headline: The talent is there. The process loses it.
intro: Training that helps employers find and fix the points where care leavers drop out of recruitment.

problem.scene: Marley, 19, is offered an interview at 9am across town.
problem.question: Payday is Friday. She can't pay the bus fare.
without: Two references and five years of addresses
with: Adverts a young person can finish alone
A named contact and a guaranteed interview
A first month that doesn't assume family
A dated pledge with named owners
problem.standards: Every council in England must publish a local offer for care leavers, including help with education, training and employment. We show employers how to get their opportunities into it.
problem.evidence: We use the Care Leaver Covenant's employer charter as a practical checklist. Signing the Covenant is your decision.

groups: HR, recruitment and early careers teams in any sector
Apprenticeship and training providers who recruit for employers
Chambers of commerce, employer networks and skills teams
Economic development, leaving care and corporate parenting leads

outcomes: Walk a recruitment process from advert to first payday and name where a family usually fills the gap.
Describe what care-experienced young people bring, and why references and an unbroken education can hide it.
Use Granovetter's research on how people hear about jobs to explain why care leavers often lack the contacts that lead to a first one.
Use Maslow to explain why travel, ID and the wait for first pay decide whether someone stays.
Rewrite an advert in clear, everyday language, with a named contact and a guaranteed interview offer.
Write a pledge for your organisation with named owners, using the Care Leaver Covenant's employer charter.

pillars.title: Where care leavers drop out of recruitment
pillars.stance_line: Recruitment quietly assumes a family in the background. These are the points where one usually fills the gap.
items: Written for someone with a person to check it. Clear words and a named contact help.
Two references and five years of addresses that many care leavers don't have to hand.
Across town at 9am, before payday. The bus fare decides whether they turn up.
Travel, ID, uniform and the weeks before the first wage.
A problem at home shows up as lateness. A buddy and a conversation come before a warning.
pillars.base: Built on Granovetter's research on how people hear about jobs (1973) and Maslow's hierarchy of needs (1943), with the Care Leaver Covenant's employer charter as a checklist.

story_line: Marley, 19, from her CV to her second week in the job, and Kyra, 21, still waiting for a call. Both are composites.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils and employers nationally on routes into work for care leavers, including Suffolk, where the council ring-fenced apprenticeships for its own care leavers, and PwC, where he brought care leavers from four councils into a global firm for the day.
He leads The Care Leaders Fellowship, a 12-month leadership programme for people solving problems for care-experienced people.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
